name: Template: climate policy and research
summary: TEMPLATE: what the charity does, the causal chain to the tonnes, the year modelled, the bottom line in years of healthy life per $1,000 (quote it live in the write-up), and the biggest uncertainty. If the result is more than ten times its cause's median on the site, say why ("more than ten times its peers because …").

source.title: charityevals' estimate: climate policy and research

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less fossil fuel near people also avoids air-pollution deaths. These rows say how much of the shared air-pollution rate applies to this charity's tonnes (docs/normalization.md 2.5); the rates themselves stay shared.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled program(s) in the year modelled
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program expenses, in US dollars, for the activities modelled below and the same year as the reach numbers (say the year in the label and the summary). Cite the audited statement of functional expenses (or the annual report) and the page. Other currencies: a row in local currency times @fx.usd_per_<cur>_<year> (the IRS yearly average, else the World Bank's; add the fact with scripts/link-fx.py), never a typed rate.

rows.label: Total expenses (all programs, management, fundraising)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: total expenses for the same year, from the same document.

rows.label: Program expenses (all programs)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: program-service expenses for the same year, from the same document.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ program expenses)
rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programs in proportion to their cost, as GiveWell and ACE do.

rows.label: Cost of the modelled program, including overhead
Tonnes of CO₂e a year the policy or technology would avert once in effect

source.title: TEMPLATE: regulatory impact assessment / modelling study

rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: emissions avoided per year once the rule, law or technology the charity works on is in effect, from the regulator's or a modelling study's estimate (cited), in tonnes of CO₂e.

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the probability that the change happens in the period because of the charity's work, from a reference class (similar rules won, similar campaigns) named here.

rows.label: Years a won reform counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (docs/normalization.md 2.9).

rows.label: Years from the grant until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the wait until the tonnes are avoided (the rule's effective date, plants re-powered, trees grown), from the policy's own dates where it has them; discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Discount for the wait until the tonnes are avoided
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate; the unit's conversion then discounts the heat deaths from the year the tonne is avoided, so nothing is discounted twice.

rows.label: Discounted years of impact
Expected tonnes averted (before adjustments)
Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the tonnes that come from burning less fuel (power, industry, transport) rather than land use, capture or methane. 0 for tonnes with no smoke.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne of this fuel, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: this fuel's and place's smoke per tonne of CO₂ against the average behind the shared rate, from per-fuel evidence (deaths per TWh, e.g. Markandya & Wilkinson 2007), not the world average.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: Read by the tco2e unit's conversion (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (none here)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: deaths a source counts directly beside the tonnes (a coal plant's own death count), per tonne brought forward, as an input with its source; 0 when the smoke is in air_pollution_weight, so nothing is counted twice.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how far the effect size above should be trusted for this charity's setting: publication bias, self-report bias, replication, differences between study populations and this program. A multiplier (1 = take the studies at face value), the product of its parts; say each part, its anchor (the same adjustment in another model of this intervention) and the range.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the outcome that would not have happened without the program (other providers, existing trends, government). Cite coverage data or trend data where possible.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: where other organisations contributed to the same outcome (co-funders, coalition campaigns, government delivery), this charity's share of everyone's spending on it. 1 when it delivers alone.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared default for this kind of work (@staff_pay.share_research_policy; facts/staff_pay.json has one per kind: goods, staff-delivered, research and policy, advocacy, media). Where the charity's financials give salaries and benefits, use them instead: an estimate input (salaries ÷ total expenses, Form 990 Part IX lines 5–9) with its source.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared pay gap for this kind of work (@staff_pay.gap_research_policy); pick the fact that fits the staff (local delivery, health and field, research and policy, advocacy, media, UK charity). Don't type a gap in.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
How much the next dollar does compared with the average dollar so far
rows.explainer: This model's cost per outcome is the charity's past spending over what it won (estimate_basis past_average), so the next dollar is valued at the shared share of the average (docs/normalization.md 2.10). 1 in `published`: what the past average itself says.
